# We Shall Build

> Through five client engagements (a build-vs-buy call made under timeline pressure for a regulated lender, BlueMoney; a founder learning to evaluate technical hires, PowerMarket; through-the-door delivery with clear documentation in a complex and ambiguous environment, Ourish; a long-term partnership refining a banking-grade email platform, Sable International; and an AI-built prototype taken safely from demo to production by deciding which AI-generated decisions survive, BauAI), one thread runs consistently: senior architectural judgement bringing engineering discipline and rigour to increasingly AI-generated codebases. What to keep, what to cut, and what will hold up in production.
>
> AI can build it fast. That's the problem.
>
> For founders and technical leads facing the decisions whose consequences are paid in time and money: build or buy, who to hire, and whether what AI built will hold. I've been making those decisions in production for twenty years.

We shall build is the public site of Vishal Shanbhag — freelance software developer and fractional CTO. Productised senior-architect engagements that start small and lead to embedded work. You don't make the wrong decision, the wrong hire, or the wrong bet on production. It usually starts with a free fifteen-minute conversation to work out whether it's worth a longer one. The site features deep-dive technical articles and the ten We shall commandments, published at https://weshall.build/en/philosophy/.

## Key pages

- [Home](https://weshall.build/): Landing page with brand positioning, engagement story cards, and service overview
- [About](https://weshall.build/en/about/): From Lehman Brothers through Inbotiqa co-founder to independent consulting
- [Services](https://weshall.build/en/services/): It starts with a conversation: a fifteen-minute call to meet, then an honest hour, a short working sprint, or ongoing monthly advisory, as far as the problem needs
- [Blog](https://weshall.build/en/blog/): Deep-dive technical analysis, operational case studies, and engineering philosophy
- [Contact](https://weshall.build/en/contact/): "Reach out." Primary path: Let's talk, a free fifteen-minute conversation with a founder-engineer, via Calendly, no pitch, no obligation. Second door: the honest hour, booked via Upwork. Writing-first is tertiary: a LinkedIn link lives in the site footer.
- [Philosophy](https://weshall.build/en/philosophy/): The ten We shall commandments — the way we build, engineering principles earned in production
- [Deutsch](https://weshall.build/de/): German locale — the site ships in English and German

## Articles

- [Bye Bye WordPress (Part 1)](https://weshall.build/en/blog/bye-bye-wordpress-part-1/): WordPress served well for a decade, but the complexity tax outweighed the convenience; switching to Jekyll and never looking back — also republished on levelup.gitconnected.com
- [ChatGPT Recommends Not Buying ChatGPT](https://weshall.build/en/blog/chatgpt-recommends-not-buying-chatgpt/): Asking ChatGPT whether its own paid plans beat the tools already in use — it advised not buying on the strength of an unmeasured promise
- [Every Few Years a Programming Language Gets a Eulogy](https://weshall.build/en/blog/every-few-years-a-programming-language-gets-a-eulogy/): Why programming languages survive or die — ecosystem, governance, and who else is forced to use yours
- [How This Site Was Built With Astro](https://weshall.build/en/blog/how-this-site-was-built/): Building weshall.build on Astro 6 with the Velocity template — the key decisions, the scorecard, and what went wrong
- [How to Choose Your Next Software Technology Stack](https://weshall.build/en/blog/how-to-choose-your-next-tech-stack/): A practical framework for technology selection, demonstrated through a real mobile-platform case study
- [One Week Agentic Development Sprint: Post Mortem](https://weshall.build/en/blog/one-week-agentic-development-sprint-post-mortem/): A seven-day agentic sprint — the engineering impressed, the intelligence wasn't validated; ten rules for the next one
- [Oops, I Deleted It Again](https://weshall.build/en/blog/oops-i-deleted-it-again/): An AI coding agent deleted raw notes without authorisation — root cause analysis of agent governance and permission models — also republished on ai.gopubby.com
- [Run Further Than a Marathon](https://weshall.build/en/blog/run-further-than-a-marathon/): A founder swaps a Forrest Gump slide for a real Indian ultra-runner and finds the metaphor he needed all along
- [Apache Solr & ZooKeeper Scaling Guidelines](https://weshall.build/en/blog/solr-zookeeper-scaling-guidelines/): Guidelines for scaling Solr and ZooKeeper deployments with high availability and disaster recovery — also republished on levelup.gitconnected.com
- [The Banyan Tree called StackOverflow is Dying](https://weshall.build/en/blog/stackoverflow-eulogy/): StackOverflow was the banyan tree at the centre of programming; the statistics tell a simple story worth acknowledging
- [To Build or Not to Build](https://weshall.build/en/blog/to-build-or-not-to-build/): When to add a feature to your product — practical decision advice from a founder and advisor
- [ZeroClaw: Zero to Super Powered Assistant](https://weshall.build/en/blog/zeroclaw-personal-ai-assistant/): Installing ZeroClaw on Kali Linux and wiring it to Discord — no cloud, no subscription leash, no data leaving your machine
